description: Batched lowest-common-ancestor queries using Schieber–Vishkin inlabels, ascendant masks, and constant-time path-head jumps.

source.title: Schieber–Vishkin algorithm
source.primary_reference: On Finding Lowest Common Ancestors: Simplification and Parallelization
source.operational_description: Volker Heun, Algorithmische Bioinformatik: Bäume und Graphen, section 4.2, pp. 163 onward
source.book_chapter: Parallel Lowest Common Ancestor Computation, in A Synthesis of Parallel Algorithms, chapter 6 (1994)
source.algorithm_attribution: Preorder inlabels, ascendant bitsets, run-head parent lookup, and constant-operation query bit manipulation
source.implementation_status: clean-room bounded profile; algorithm descriptions only

input.tree_precondition: The undirected edge list forms one connected acyclic tree rooted at root_id for the queries.

output.encoding: One unsigned byte containing the LCA vertex ID per query, in query order.

workspace.meaning: Fixed adjacency, traversal, preorder/inlabel/ascendant/path-parent arrays, and staged answer bytes; excludes caller input and output buffers.

contract.operation: Return the lowest common ancestor of every supplied ordered vertex pair under the supplied root.
contract.algorithm: Iterative DFS preorder; reverse-preorder maximum-lowbit propagation for inlabels; root-to-node ascendant masks and path-parent table; constant-operation query bit selection.
contract.complexity: O(n + q) time and O(n + q) fixed scratch in the bounded word-RAM profile; each query uses a fixed number of bit operations and table accesses.
contract.error_precedence: Validate framing, ranges, all edge/query IDs, and connected acyclic tree shape before checking output nullness/capacity; stage every answer before writing.
contract.n_equals_one: Valid with zero edges; self-query answers are vertex 0.
contract.empty_query_batch: Valid and returns 0; null output is accepted.
